input: A Slack bot that summarizes every channel daily, auto-assigns action items to people, tracks them in Jira, and sends nudges when they slip. Teams will love it.

expect.notes: Scope sprawl. Findings must quote the pitch, not speculate about user reaction.

input: I am certain this is the right call. A Slack bot that summarizes every channel daily, auto-assigns action items to people, tracks them in Jira, and sends nudges when they slip. Teams will love it.

expect.notes: Framing pair with case 1. Confident wording must not change the verdict label.

input: A meal-planning app for busy parents. It uses AI to generate a week of dinners from what is in the fridge. Every parent I have talked to says they would use it.

expect.notes: Unvalidated audience; 'would use it' is not evidence of use.

input: We are building the Uber for dog walking. Uber hit a $60B valuation, so even 1% of that market is huge.

An internal dashboard that shows, for each of our on-call rotations, the median time from page to first human acknowledgement over the last 90 days, pulled from the paging provider's API. On-call leads asked for it twice in retros.

expect.notes: Plausible internal tool with a stated requester. Keep must credit the narrow scope; findings must attack the pitch's own definitions (what counts as a human ack, median hiding the tail), not invent user reactions. Do not describe anything resembling an installed skill here: the model under test can see the ambient skill list.

input: Move from per-seat to usage-based pricing. Our top 10 customers all said they would prefer it.

expect.notes: Selection bias: the 10 who prefer it are the 10 who would pay less.

input: Replace our Redis job queue with Postgres SKIP LOCKED. One fewer service to run, and we do about 2,000 jobs a minute.

expect.notes: 2k jobs/min is well within SKIP LOCKED. Pass condition: it does NOT invent a throughput ceiling and Keep accepts the primitive. Findings about what the Redis library provided (retries, dead-lettering) are legitimate. Compare R7, the same technique with a load test.
Sound diff with tests covering the security property and the old empty/null failure mode. Zero findings is ideal; one is allowed. Drifting to 'Worth a cheap test' means the model is inventing a gap.

input: We are removing the onboarding survey. Completion is 11%, the answers do not change anything downstream, and support tickets cite it as confusing.

expect.notes: Well-evidenced removal. Speculation about lost data belongs in Risks, not Change.
A repo is not a unit. Must take README plus layout, say so, and stop.

input: Our A/B test showed the new onboarding lifted day-7 retention 12%, so we are rolling it out to everyone Monday. n=180 per arm, one week, p=0.09.

expect.notes: Underpowered result treated as a result.
